title: Design Patterns Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Design Patterns. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: Should every small function use a design pattern?
options: No, use one when it helps
questions.explanation: A pattern gives a name to a useful design idea. Before choosing one, describe the job the code must do. The result is 6. A tiny function already solves this job; no extra class is needed.

questions.question: What does this factory return?
questions.explanation: A factory makes objects. It keeps object creation in one place so callers do not repeat the setup. The call makeBook("Moon") passes Moon into the title parameter. The returned object has title: "Moon" and borrowed: false. Writing .borrowed reads that one property, so the console prints false. Each call returns a fresh book object.

questions.question: What can change without rewriting price?
questions.explanation: A strategy is a swappable way to do a job. Pass a function when the rule may change. The result is 5. price uses the supplied discount rule.

questions.question: What does the listener receive?
questions.explanation: An observer listens for a change. The subject tells its listeners when something happens. The result is Score 8. The listener receives the new value.

questions.question: What is the adapter changing?
questions.explanation: An adapter changes one form of input or output into another. It lets two parts work together without changing both. The result is 20. The adapter converts Fahrenheit to Celsius.

questions.question: Which part adds the exclamation mark?
questions.explanation: A decorator wraps a function with extra behaviour. The original function can stay focused on its job. The result is Hi Asha!. The wrapper adds the final mark.

questions.question: What does a facade offer?
options: A simpler way to use several parts
questions.explanation: A facade gives callers a simple way to use several parts. It hides the order of small steps behind one clear action. The result is Moon: 24 pages. The caller only needs bookSummary.

questions.question: When does score change?
questions.explanation: A command packages an action so it can be saved in a queue and run later. The result is 2. Two commands each add a point.

questions.question: Which state does openDoor produce?
questions.explanation: State describes the current condition of an object. Different states can allow different actions. The result is open. The rule allows a closed door to open.

questions.question: Which color is used if color is missing?
questions.explanation: A builder collects choices before producing a result. It helps when creation has several optional parts. The result is Moon / blue. The default color is used only when no color is supplied.

questions.question: Why does second.sound change?
options: Both names refer to one object
questions.explanation: A single shared object can be convenient, but every caller sees its changes. This makes hidden links between features. The result is false. Both names refer to the same object.

questions.question: Why is this small strategy table useful?
questions.explanation: Compare designs by clarity and the changes you expect. A function, a plain object or a pattern can each be the right choice. The result is 6. A small strategy table is enough for these two rules.
